audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and breakdown.early frame the lane as 'he wins the lane, you win the map' — against Vladimir the opposite is true: TF wins the early lane (content layer, packet chart and 50.37% WR all agree), Vlad takes over at first item.
audit.why: Vladimir is push-limited and sustain-less before Q ranks; TF's Blue/Red Card poke and shove dominate 1-3. The full layer carried the generic anti-mage template.
audit.corrected: tldr and breakdown.early rewritten to the actual shape: win early, roam at 6, close before his AP item spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full phases[].side disagreed with content win[] on rows 0,1,2,3,4,6. Content matches the packet levelChart (TF 1-3, Skill 4-5, TF 6, Vlad first item, Skill late). Also whys[4] said 'At 5' for the Level 6 row.
audit.why: TF's spikes: levels 1-3 poke/shove, Destiny at 6; Vlad's spike is first AP item when Q sustain ramps (9s to 4.6s CD) and late Hemoplague scaling.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved to agree with content; whys rewritten per verdict; whys[4] level typo fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers; dos/donts bullets were tradeGood/tradeBad pasted verbatim; Sanguine Pool's 2s untargetability and 28s rank-1 cooldown never stated concretely.
audit.why: Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s with 2s untargetable — that downtime is TF's whole commit window and dodges gold card (missingInteractions confirms). Anti-heal timing already covered in report[8].
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns added; bullets rewritten to Pool-baiting and Q-sustain specifics.

edits.before: He wins the lane on paper — you win the map on schedule. Farm, lock cards defensively, and make 6 the whole story.
edits.after: You win the lane early — he wins the game late. Shove, poke, roam on 6, and close before his first big AP item lands.

edits.before: Farm, lock defensively, and watch the clock — pre-6 TF is a savings bond. Your job is reaching Destiny with the deck intact.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours: Vladimir is push-limited before Q ranks — shove with Red Card, chip with Blue Card, punish his last-hits.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by dodging your gold card with Sanguine Pool and out-sustaining your poke once Q healing ramps.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W gold card like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — 28s at rank 1, 16s max, 2s untargetable. Bait it before you spend the kill window; commit in the downtime. - His Q falls from 9s to 4.6s with ranks — the sustain ramps, so cash your trades early.

edits.before: Lock gold off-screen, walk up once, card-auto-Q, and leave — one stun-chunk per cycle is all the lane asks of you.
edits.after: Hold yellow for his Q step-up — Transfusion is point-and-click, so the stun is the only price you can put on his walk forward.

edits.before: Cycling cards inside his engage range for stacked-deck greed — TF dies in exactly one mistimed auto-walk per game; don't pre-book it.
edits.after: Vlad answers ganks with a 2-second untargetable Pool — your leads come from Destiny cross-maps, not from grinding his sustain mid.

edits.before: Q-farm from range and concede the duel question entirely — your level 1 is a wallet, not a weapon.
edits.after: Vladimir starts weak and push-limited — Blue Card poke and a free shove make level 1 yours from the first wave.

edits.before: W online: the gold card re-prices his every step-up. Lock yellow when he walks forward and the lane behaves.
edits.after: W online: Wild Cards shove plus the stun threat keeps him pinned and low — the lane is yours to bully here.

edits.before: Full kit: stacked-deck autos plus card cycling is a real short trade — but your game is the clock, not the lane.
edits.after: Full kit: stacked-deck autos plus card cycling bully him before his Q sustain ramps — keep chipping him down.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q the wave, lock cards on cooldown, and watch side lanes like they're your KDA.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out — his Transfusion healing starts closing your poke while you shove and eye side lanes.

edits.before: Destiny online — THE level in this lane. Every shove is now a bot-lane death sentence with a 130-second timer.
edits.after: Destiny online — THE level: his Hemoplague is a teamfight tool, not a lane answer, so every shove pays cross-map.

edits.before: Late TF is a coin with two good sides: split the side lane R-safe, or hold Destiny as the pick-and-collapse button.
edits.after: Late is even: his Hemoplague AoE and Pool escape trade off against your picks — split R-safe or hold Destiny to collapse.

edits.before: At 5 you retain the roam-tempo edge with Destiny before his item spike.
edits.after: At 6 you retain the roam-tempo edge with Destiny before his item spike.

notes: Both suspectNames are false positives: 'Gold Card' is TF's own W yellow card, 'Sanguine Pool' is Vladimir's real W. Content chart already matched the packet, so full-layer side edits alone are correct per the chart rule (no win[] edits). Anti-heal timing (missingInteractions) is already present in report[8].t ('Add anti-heal early into his sustain') — no edit needed.
